verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā lakuṇḍakabhaddiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then Venerable Bhaddiya the Dwarf went to see the Buddha.

verses.pali: Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ lakuṇḍakabhaddiyaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
verses.english: The Buddha saw him coming off in the distance,

verses.pali: “passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṁ bhikkhuṁ āgacchantaṁ dubbaṇṇaṁ duddasikaṁ okoṭimakaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ paribhūtarūpan”ti?
verses.english: “Mendicants, do you see this monk coming—ugly, unsightly, deformed, and despised by the mendicants?”

verses.pali: “Eso kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo, na ca sā samāpatti sulabharūpā yā tena bhikkhunā asamāpannapubbā.
verses.english: “That mendicant is very mighty and powerful. It’s not easy to find an attainment that he has not already attained.

verses.pali: Yassa catthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti.
verses.english: And he has realized the supreme end of the spiritual path in this very life. He lives having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.”
That is what the Buddha said.
Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
though their bodies are not equal,
if a little person is wise,
not the fool with a good body.”
